cases.purpose: Observe actual default/permissive/restricted KEXINIT MAC bytes, retain full allowed encrypted commands and supported disallowed refusal for hmac-sha2-256,hmac-sha2-512.
cases.oracle: Independent OpenSSH client/server and RFC4253 sections6/7.1/7.3. A byte-preserving loopback relay retains both entire initial streams, exact packet offsets, lengths, padding and hashes. The guarded parser reads version/clear packets and10 name-lists, validates reserved/tail fields, and stops each direction at NEWKEYS; following bytes remain opaque. All peers force non-AEAD aes256-ctr and curve25519-sha256; the actual separate MAC must appear in both raw proposals and client negotiated-direction diagnostics. Setup ssh-Q checks the real client supports both MACs, then OpenSSH independently proves default-allowed, permissive-allowed, permissive-other and restricted-allowed encrypted commands, plus actual restricted-other MAC mismatch/refusal. Candidate repeats all5 probes using fresh fixture keys and strict known_hosts. Standard preserves the revision98 MAC choices; etm exercises another source-advertised real-MAC framing path. Neither variant substitutes implicit AEAD authentication for the MAC requirement.
cases.comparison: Exact ordered booleans distinguish advertisement, clear KEX/ECDH/NEWKEYS progress, full encrypted auth/command and policy. Successful encrypted command requires status0, exact marker/stdout, strict fixture host-key verification, authenticated client log and expected non-AEAD cipher/real MAC in both directions. Refusal requires255, the matching MAC diagnostic, both raw MAC intersections empty, other KEX/cipher intersections still valid, no NEWKEYS or command marker. Full policy boolean is gated by successful default, both permissive MACs and restricted-allowed encrypted commands. Raw proposal filtering/early refusal cannot pass that gate if a baseline encryption path fails. Normal server exits, relay thread cleanup and no forced kills remain required. Server phase ports differ; readiness needs the exact Popen child alive plus its own post-bind announcement and the loopback listener, preventing the stale-listener problem observed in109.
